title: Temporal integration in human auditory cortex is predominantly yoked to absolute time
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Predict the source untied integration-window estimates from the opposite nonoverlapping-segment split, retaining those target estimates unchanged across candidates.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Predict the source untied integration-window estimates from the opposite nonoverlapping-segment split, retaining those target estimates unchanged across candidates.

Source-paper comparison for Original fixed-untied-target cross-split Spearman correlation: Spearman rank correlation of predictor estimates with the fixed source opposite-split untied estimates; higher is better for this noisy-target agreement task, not demonstrated ground-truth accuracy.
success_criteria: Verify admissibility of the original fixed-target prediction route and bind the exact source splits, cohort, preprocessing and correlation reduction.
Freeze opposite-split untied target arrays independently of the candidate; candidates must never redefine both sides of the correlation.
Recover or rerun the source tied predictor with the identical target and show improvement over its source-reported 0.668 anchor using justified effect and uncertainty criteria.
Do not substitute tied/tied 0.716, a biological yoking effect, new holdout split or correlation reconstruction as success.
Freeze access/resource budgets, method and preprocessing before final scoring; claims remain about noisy-target prediction unless independent truth evidence exists.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
